summary: The root دعع (daʿʿa) primarily means to push or repel with force, often with a shove or thrust. It implies a strong, sometimes violent, expulsion or driving away.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.gloss: He pushed him, thrust him; drove him, away; he repelled him; he did so harshly, roughly

parts.t: drove him, away; he repelled him:
That is he who pusheth, thrusteth,
who treateth the orphan with harshness, roughness,
driving, away; and chiding with rudeness,
(Z, TA.) And in like manner, in the same [lii. 13],
On the day when they shall be pushed,
violence, to the fire of Hell.

headwords.def: دَعَّهُ دع دعه دعة ودع , aor. دَعُعَ , (S, Z,) inf. n. دَعٌّ , (S, K,) He pushed him, thrust him, or drove him, away; he repelled him: (S:) or he did so harshly, roughly, or violently. (A'Obeyd, K.) Hence, in the Kur [cvii. 2], فَذٰلِكَ الَّذِى يَدُعُّ اليَتِيمَ That is he who pusheth, thrusteth, or driveth, away the orphan: (S:) or, who doth so harshly, roughly, or violently: (Bd, Jel:) or, who treateth the orphan with harshness, roughness, or violence; pushing, thrusting, or driving, away; and chiding with rudeness, or coarseness. (Z, TA.) And in like manner, in the same [lii. 13], يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَى نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا On the day when they shall be pushed, or thrust, or driven, with harshness, roughness, or violence, to the fire of Hell.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
